newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: SOCCER-"INDOMITABLE LIONS" HUMILIATED IN COSTA RICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-"INDOMITABLE LIONS" HUMILIATED IN COSTA RICA.

text.p: Cameroon's players initially refused to take the pitch for a friendly with Costa Rica on Sunday because of a dispute over money.
When they finally agreed to play they were hammered 5-0.
Striker Paulo Cesar Wanchope scored a first half hat-trick as the so-called "Indomitable Lions", who set pulses racing in the 1990 World Cup, capitulated meekly against unrated opponents.

Cameroon's players had claimed they were owed $35,000 from television rights and were prepared to boycott the match. But after intensive negotiations they finally lined up 45 minutes late, only to be outclassed.

Two second half goals by Austin Berry completed Cameroon's misery and gave Costa Rica an ideal work-out for next week's home match with Mexico, their first in the final stages of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers.
Since 1990, Cameroon soccer has been plagued by political bickering and the team's fortunes have taken a turn for the worse.
They were knocked out of the 1994 World Cup in the first round and failed to reach the last eight of last year's African Nations' Cup.
FIFA threatened to ban them after a government minister suspended the Cameroon soccer federation.
Last month, FIFA stepped in again when it ordered Cameroon directors to pay former national team goalkeeper Joseph-Antoine Bell money he was owed for taking part in the 1990 World Cup.
Cameroon were labelled violent by Brazil coach Mario Zagallo after losing 2-0 in a friendly last year and were held 0-0 at home by Angola in their most recent World Cup qualifier.
